1Jwo5qc78QU.summary: Tom Scott's long explainer on YouTube's copyright system, Content ID and the DMCA. He argues the platform's system is a workaround for a broader copyright system that does not fit the modern world.
1Jwo5qc78QU.why: The default link in copyright and takedown threads, recommended as an excellent, comprehensive explanation of why automated enforcement and the law work as they do.

1OfxlSG6q5Y.summary: Technology Connections takes apart a 1940s Sunbeam Radiant Control toaster. It senses the toast's own browning and lowers and raises it automatically using purely mechanical parts and no electronics.
1OfxlSG6q5Y.why: HN returns to it again and again as a favorite example of elegant, chip-free mechanical engineering that beats modern toasters.

1gEz__sMVaY.summary: James D'Angelo argues that the 1970 Legislative Reorganization Act made congressional votes public, opening the door to lobbyists and special interests. He proposes restoring secret voting as a cheap fix for corruption and many social ills.
1gEz__sMVaY.why: HN commenters recommend it as a long, evidence-backed theory for what changed in the 1970s and why Congress is broken, even when they are unsure they agree.

1ffBJ4sVUb4.summary: A Linux.conf.au 2013 talk that explains git's internal model using a playful, toy-based approach. It presents git operations as operations on a graph of commits, aimed at people who find git confusing.
1ffBJ4sVUb4.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as the talk that finally makes git's data model click for beginners, despite its odd title.

15RTC22Z2xI.summary: James Mickens of Harvard gives a funny lecture at HBS's Future Assembly arguing that blockchains are a very bad idea. He covers their trust, legal and practical shortcomings for real-world problems.
15RTC22Z2xI.why: A staple HN recommendation in crypto and Web3 threads as an entertaining, compelling case against blockchain.

1TKSfAkWWN0.summary: Veritasium explains magnetism as a consequence of special relativity. Length contraction of moving charges makes a current in a wire attract or repel a nearby moving charge.
1TKSfAkWWN0.why: HN commenters recommend it as a short, clear explanation of why moving charges create magnetic fields.

1-dUkyn_fZA.summary: John Kitchin shows how Emacs org-mode with Python lets researchers combine narrative, math, figures and executable code in one document. It exports to LaTeX, HTML and PDF, and he used it for papers and e-books.
1-dUkyn_fZA.why: Repeatedly recommended as the canonical demo of org-mode for literate programming and reproducible research.

1MGjFKs9bnU.summary: A documentary on the last day the New York Times was printed with linotype machines in 1978, following the process from the newsroom to the press. It marks the move to computerized typesetting.
1MGjFKs9bnU.why: Frequently recommended as an absorbing look at hot-metal typesetting and the end of the linotype era.

1qSTcxt2t74.summary: Captain Disillusion's comedic talk at the 2018 Blender Conference recounts how he uses Blender as a production tool for his VFX-debunking web series. It is part case study and part love letter to the Blender community.
1qSTcxt2t74.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining and inspiring Blender talk, and often links it in threads about learning Blender.

1e8VZlPBx_0.summary: Part two of Alan Kay's Stanford Startup School lecture on inventing the future. He draws on his time at Xerox PARC and elsewhere to discuss how to think about new technology and what makes ideas useful.
1e8VZlPBx_0.why: Frequently suggested in Ask HN threads on finding ideas, creativity and why incumbents like Xerox missed what they invented.

1bNOO3xxMc0.summary: Zach Tellman's Clojure West talk covers the basics of queueing theory and its practical use in systems, including backpressure, how queues break down under load, and pitfalls of naive core.async use.
1bNOO3xxMc0.why: HN recommends it as a fascinating explanation of queues, flow control and overload that applies well beyond Clojure.

1PhArSujR_A.summary: Part 4 of John Carmack's QuakeCon 2013 keynote, covering OpenGL, functional programming, Haskell, Lisp and Scheme, typing, multithreading, events and garbage collection.
1PhArSujR_A.why: Cited again and again as Carmack's key public statement on functional programming and purity in game development, plus his remarks on garbage collection.

1jHUY3qoBu8.summary: Imphenzia's 83-minute tutorial covers the low poly modeling techniques he learned over five years of Blender use, with timestamps from navigation and extrusion onward. It uses Blender 2.83 with default keys.
1jHUY3qoBu8.why: It is the most-recommended beginner Blender tutorial on HN, with several people saying it made them comfortable in a couple of hours.

1uflg7LDmzI.summary: James Mickens's 2015 Harvard colloquium argues that browsers are bloated and insecure because feature races trump clean interface design. He presents a cleaner, more secure browser architecture (Atlantis) with a much smaller API surface.
1uflg7LDmzI.why: HN cites it whenever people discuss rebuilding the web platform or what a better browser architecture could look like.

1xQeXOz0Ncs.summary: Nickolas Means recounts the 1979 Three Mile Island accident minute by minute, from the control rod insertion to the operator's decision to switch off emergency cooling. He argues that finding systemic causes is more useful than blaming individuals.
1xQeXOz0Ncs.why: HN recommends it whenever a failure is blamed on human error, as a clear case study in looking for the systemic second story.

15_-hgsX2V0.summary: The author of copyparty introduces the FOSS file server he has built over five years, demoing its features such as resumable uploads, WebDAV and deduplication. The video itself is shown running on a demo server.
15_-hgsX2V0.why: HN commenters call it a model demo video and the quickest way to see how much one developer packed into a self-hosted file server.

1K5oDtVAYzk.summary: CGP Grey explains that postal codes are routing instructions for mail rather than geographic regions. He looks at the quirks and problems this causes.
1K5oDtVAYzk.why: HN recommends it whenever zip codes, addresses or geospatial data come up, as a clear explanation of the hidden pattern in post codes.

1L2ef1CP-yw.summary: Matthias Wandel uses anemometer measurements to find where to place a fan to move the most air through a house at night. He finds that placing the fan some distance back from the window works better.
1L2ef1CP-yw.why: Cited in cooling and fan-noise threads as a short video with actual data on fan placement.

1H3xQaf7BFI.summary: A Gamers Nexus investigative documentary on the black market for Nvidia AI GPUs, following smugglers, middlemen, and buyers, including reporting from China. It examines how export-restricted chips reach their users.
1H3xQaf7BFI.why: HN recommends it as real on-the-ground reporting on how banned GPUs get into China despite export controls.

1Y1ya-yF35g.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on the US nuclear arsenal and how poorly it is maintained and secured. It covers weapons accidents, outdated launch protocols and security problems.
1Y1ya-yF35g.why: HN recommends it as a funny but sobering overview of nuclear weapons safety failures.

1rZ-JorHJEY.summary: A roughly hour-long live hacking session in which Go team members Andrew Gerrand and Brad Fitzpatrick write the new version of tip.golang.org, the site serving leading-edge Go documentation. It is unedited pair programming on a real Go project.
1rZ-JorHJEY.why: HN people point to it as a rare chance to watch skilled developers write real code live, pair programming and explaining as they go.

1wAaI_6b9JE.summary: Matt Parker gives a hands-on Royal Institution talk on how four-dimensional shapes appear in a 3D world, with props like straw frames, Mobius strips and a knitted hat. It is a playful general-audience tour of the fourth dimension.
1wAaI_6b9JE.why: Recommended as an enjoyable, accessible talk for building intuition about higher dimensions.

15R2pMqU2ok.summary: A Huberman Lab podcast episode on the gut-brain axis and how the gut microbiome affects the nervous system, hunger and overall health. It covers the pathways by which the gut influences the brain and practical steps for gut health.
15R2pMqU2ok.why: Recommended as an accessible neuroscientist's overview of gut microbiome science with practical takeaways.

17KCHwOwgms.summary: Dan Abramov's talk on the wet codebase, using visualizations to show how removing all duplication too early produces wrong abstractions that are hard to unwind.
17KCHwOwgms.why: Recommended in DRY versus duplication debates for its visuals and its case that copy/paste can beat a wrong abstraction.

17oCQakzIl8.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on the Chinese government's treatment of the Uighur people, covering the human rights abuses in Xinjiang and why they deserve attention.
17oCQakzIl8.why: HN points to it as an accessible, well-made mix of education and entertainment for anyone wanting to understand the Xinjiang situation.

1L3eeC2lJZs.summary: Alamo Drafthouse posted an angry voicemail from a customer who was kicked out for texting in the theater. The theater turned it into a humorous in-house preview.
1L3eeC2lJZs.why: It is cited as a viral example of Alamo enforcing its no-talking and no-texting rules with humor.

1W_mSOS1Qts.summary: A long Gamers Nexus investigation into how volatile US tariffs affect the computer hardware industry. It interviews manufacturers and sellers about costs, margins and why moving production to the US is hard.
1W_mSOS1Qts.why: HN recommends it for concrete numbers on what tariffs do to small hardware businesses.

1WupH8oyrAo.summary: A one-minute clip of a crow repeatedly sliding down a snowy roof on a small lid, apparently just for fun.
1WupH8oyrAo.why: Offered as vivid evidence that animals, crows in particular, play for pleasure and display intelligence beyond survival needs.

1tSqSMOyNFE.summary: A short Veritasium video explaining regression to the mean and how ignoring it leads to wrong conclusions about punishment versus reward, medical treatments and sports streaks. It uses the example of flight instructors who believed criticism works better than praise.
1tSqSMOyNFE.why: HN commenters link it as the clearest short explanation of regression to the mean, especially for how it misleads people about feedback and statistics.

14wqBA5Q1yc.summary: SethBling performs the first credits warp in Super Mario World on a real SNES console, a glitch that plays the ending without beating Bowser. The run relies on pixel-perfect positioning and tools such as a helper ROM hack.
14wqBA5Q1yc.why: Cited as a landmark of speedrunning, where a trick once limited to tool-assisted runs was pulled off live on hardware.

17jymDn0W6U.summary: The American Museum of Natural History's film flies from the Himalayas out through the atmosphere and solar system to the afterglow of the Big Bang, using its Digital Universe Atlas four-dimensional map.
17jymDn0W6U.why: HN people share it as an eye-opening, moving visualization of the scale of the universe.

1Evwgu369Jw.summary: A short animated RSA piece with Dr Brene Brown's voiceover on the difference between empathy and sympathy. She argues that real connection requires getting in touch with your own vulnerability, rather than trying to fix someone's pain.
1Evwgu369Jw.why: Recommended as a quick, memorable explanation of how to support someone in pain without making it about yourself.

1Hqm0dYKUx4.summary: A minutephysics video explaining why a piano cannot be perfectly tuned, comparing equal temperament with just intonation and the math of harmonics.
1Hqm0dYKUx4.why: Commenters link it as a quick, clear explanation of why twelve notes only approximate simple ratios.

1OEu9C51K2A.summary: Bjarne Stroustrup's CppCon 2015 keynote on using C++14 to write better code, not just different code. It introduces the C++ Core Guidelines and the machine-checkable rules and GSL library behind them.
1OEu9C51K2A.why: HN people recommend it as the starting point for modern C++ and for the language's safety story.

1hs451PfFzQ.summary: Linkus7 explains how a community reverse-engineered The Wind Waker to predict its random number generator and beat the Sploosh Kaboom battleship minigame consistently. It includes d3 animations by Peter Schmidt-Nielsen.
1hs451PfFzQ.why: HN recommends it as a rigorous, fun example of reverse engineering a game to predict and conquer its RNG.

1sl5KJ69qiA.summary: Vsauce's Michael Stevens stages a realistic version of the trolley problem with unsuspecting subjects who believe they must decide a life-or-death outcome. The Mind Field episode compares what people say they would do with what they actually do.
1sl5KJ69qiA.why: Recommended as a worthwhile real-world experiment whenever trolley problems or moral dilemmas come up.

13eiDhuvM6Y.summary: Coffeezilla investigates Counter-Strike skin gambling, the role of Valve and the legal and PR response, including effects on minors.
13eiDhuvM6Y.why: Pointed to in threads on CS skin economy and Valve as an investigation arguing Valve is complicit in underage gambling.

1PGm8LslEb4.summary: Part 1 of Smarter Every Day's three-part series on manipulating the YouTube algorithm. It features Renee DiResta and examples of how social media platforms can be manipulated.
1PGm8LslEb4.why: Referenced in threads on social media manipulation and junk content as an interesting miniseries, though one commenter criticized its ExpressVPN ad read.

1Y1kJpHBn50.summary: A Wendover Productions explainer on how airport security is designed, covering screening layers, x-ray scanning, and the contrast with Israel's profiling-based approach. It walks through the logic behind why security works the way it does.
1Y1kJpHBn50.why: HN commenters point to it as a well-researched primer when airport security theatre and Israeli-style screening come up.

1b-bijO3uEw.summary: A 1080p widescreen capture of the Deus Ex conversation between JC Denton and the AI Morpheus. It is a philosophical exchange that includes surveillance as a replacement for God.
1b-bijO3uEw.why: Commenters call it one of the game's best dialogues and bring it up in discussions of mass surveillance.

1f6YyH62jFE.summary: A 37C3 talk by Kaspersky researchers on Operation Triangulation, a zero-click iPhone attack that targeted their own colleagues. They describe capturing every stage of the chain, four zero-days and a previously unknown spyware active for years.
1f6YyH62jFE.why: HN recommends it as a gripping look at what nation-state attackers can do, used as the primary source in threads about iPhone security and Kaspersky.

1sd26pWhfmg.summary: Nicholas Carlini of Anthropic talks at [un]prompted 2026 about how adversaries could misuse current LLMs for attacks. He shows recent models finding zero-day vulnerabilities in heavily tested software, including a SQL injection in Ghost.
1sd26pWhfmg.why: HN cites it as a concrete demonstration that LLMs have suddenly become strong at finding and exploiting vulnerabilities.

13cmHf_kt-Q.summary: Stuart Sierra presents the Component library for Clojure, a way to manage stateful services like database connections and thread pools without global mutable state. He draws on both functional and object-oriented principles.
13cmHf_kt-Q.why: Pointed to as a thought-provoking talk on structuring large systems, including outside Clojure.

144uOfr4SYA.summary: A Munk Debate on the proposition that AI research and development poses an existential threat. Yoshua Bengio and Max Tegmark argue for it, and Melanie Mitchell and Yann LeCun argue against.
144uOfr4SYA.why: HN commenters recommend it as a good debate with leading figures on both sides of the AI existential risk question.

160F8F8mXlo.summary: Alex O'Connor shows that ChatGPT cannot draw a wine glass filled to the brim, and ties the failure to David Hume's missing shade of blue. It asks what the failure says about how image models learn.
160F8F8mXlo.why: HN treats it as the origin of the full-wine-glass meme and an illustration of how models lack concepts missing from their training data.

1AcEt073Uds.summary: Louis Rossmann argues that reballing flip-chip GPUs is not a real fix for dead laptop GPUs. He explains why such repairs and oven reflow tricks fail and what is actually happening with failing hardware.
1AcEt073Uds.why: HN people cite it to debunk oven-reflow and reballing repair folklore, and as part of Rossmann's critiques of Apple hardware quality.

1AjhFZVfB9c.summary: Timothy Baldridge presents Pixie, a lightweight Lisp built on RPython, at Strange Loop 2015. It covers C interop, immutable data structures, fast startup and async-by-default IO.
1AjhFZVfB9c.why: HN mentions it as the author's own overview of Pixie, with an interesting implementation technique near the end.

1EWQYAfuMYw.summary: Lyle Bickley of the PDP-1 restoration team tours the 1959 DEC machine at the Computer History Museum and plays the original Spacewar! He covers its graphics display and the MIT student programs written for it.
1EWQYAfuMYw.why: Linked in Spacewar and vintage computing threads as a charming demo on real hardware.

1Nh_vxpycEA.summary: Tom Scott features Kurtis Baute inside a sealed homemade biodome as carbon dioxide builds up, showing how stale air with elevated CO2 affects cognitive function. Sources include studies on CO2 and cognitive scores.
1Nh_vxpycEA.why: HN links it as a popular, accessible introduction to indoor CO2 and its effect on thinking, in air quality threads.

1YFrISfN7jo.summary: PBS Space Time explains how spacetime geometry and light cones determine the order of events and what can cause what. It visualizes causality in special relativity.
1YFrISfN7jo.why: Used as a go-to reference for relativity arguments, such as spacetime intervals being the same for all observers, and as a suggested follow-up for physics fans.

1YbcB6b4A2U.summary: Lex Fridman interviews Bryan Johnson, founder of Kernel and previously Braintree, about brain-computer interfaces and Kernel's non-invasive brain monitoring hardware. It covers what the devices can do today and the company's plans.
1YbcB6b4A2U.why: Cited as an accessible overview of Kernel's technology whenever its brain-sensing helmets come up.

1bO8zEaSuWg.summary: Tom Scott explains how in Norway and other Nordic countries tax returns, and so individual incomes, are public. He looks at the effects of wage transparency and whether it is a good idea, with sources listed in the description.
1bO8zEaSuWg.why: HN points to it in discussions of salary transparency as a short, well-sourced overview of how public tax records work in Nordic countries.

1faaOrtHJ-A.summary: Pat Wyatt, a veteran game programmer who worked at Blizzard and ArenaNet, speaks at HandmadeCon 2015 in a conversation with Casey Muratori. He discusses network code and architecture in games he worked on, including mistakes on Diablo and the success of Guild Wars.
1faaOrtHJ-A.why: HN points to it as a first-hand account of game netcode and engineering lessons from a Blizzard and Guild Wars developer.

1rCrfQUcXDI.summary: Part two of EEVblog's visit to the NASA/CSIRO Canberra Deep Space Communication Complex, showing the control room and how operators contact Voyager 2. It includes live data and spectrum displays.
1rCrfQUcXDI.why: Commenters recommend the series for hearing an operations supervisor explain how Voyager signals are actually received.

1RLdSvQ-OF0.summary: Gregory Chaitin is interviewed on Closer To Truth about whether mathematics is invented or discovered. He gives a nuanced view that ties the question to the nature of reality.
1RLdSvQ-OF0.why: HN commenters recommend it as a thoughtful and nuanced take on the philosophy of mathematics.

1VPfZ_XzisU.summary: Veritasium explains the Dzhanibekov effect, also called the tennis racket theorem, where a spinning object flips unexpectedly about its intermediate axis. The video gives an intuitive account of the underlying rotational dynamics, drawing on Terry Tao's explanation and the original papers.
1VPfZ_XzisU.why: HN people cite it as the clearest layperson-friendly explanation of rotational instability whenever spinning bodies, tumbling objects or axis shifts come up.

1iAJPoc23-M.summary: Hyperland is a 1990 BBC documentary written by and starring Douglas Adams, who tours an imagined future of hypertext and software agents. It features Ted Nelson among others.
1iAJPoc23-M.why: Treated as a remarkable early look at ideas like hypertext, agents and the web before they existed.

1-vcErOPofQ.summary: Grace Hopper appears on Letterman and uses a foot-long piece of wire to show how far light travels in a nanosecond.
1-vcErOPofQ.why: Brought up whenever latency, light speed or the size of a nanosecond comes up, as the classic physical demonstration.

10qowKUW82U.summary: An interview with Anders Hejlsberg, lead architect of TypeScript, about porting the TypeScript compiler to Go. He covers the 10x type-checking speedup, lower memory use, and why Go was chosen.
10qowKUW82U.why: HN points to it as the authoritative answer to why the team picked Go rather than C# or Rust, citing timestamps on cyclic data structures and garbage collection.

13Ah9ES2yTU.summary: Mark Bittman and baker Jim Lahey of Sullivan Street Bakery demonstrate the no-knead bread recipe, where a long, slow rise does the work instead of kneading. It is a short New York Times recipe video.
13Ah9ES2yTU.why: HN people point to it as a cheap, low-effort way to bake very good bread and as a beginner step into cooking.

19zm1Fn0S9M.summary: Robert Moss's JuliaCon 2015 talk describes using Julia as a specification language for ACAS X, the next-generation airborne collision avoidance system that succeeds TCAS.
19zm1Fn0S9M.why: HN points to it as a real-world example of Julia used in safety-critical aerospace design.

1BbMBdGPoHM.summary: Marshall Kirk McKusick gives a talk at EuroBSDCon tracing filesystem and storage development from 1979 to today, using the BSD Fast Filesystem as the focus. It covers early disk-geometry optimization through later contiguous layout and small-file performance work.
1BbMBdGPoHM.why: Pointed to as the authoritative history of FFS from one of its original creators.

1FXuMs6YRCY.summary: Ben Felix rebuts common arguments for holding only US stocks, such as past outperformance and international revenue exposure. He supports the case for international diversification with cited academic research.
1FXuMs6YRCY.why: Cited in investing threads as a research-backed argument for diversifying beyond US equities, with sources in the description.

1GhNXHCQGsM.summary: A demo of PREDATOR (TLD), a real-time object tracker that learns the appearance of its target and improves while it tracks. The technology was later developed commercially.
1GhNXHCQGsM.why: HN found it a nifty demo and cites it as a primitive but effective learning tracker that predates modern deep-learning trackers.

1J9LOqiXdpE.summary: Climate Town argues that the personal carbon footprint idea shifts blame to individuals and traces it to oil company marketing, urging collective and political action.
1J9LOqiXdpE.why: Cited in discussions of carbon footprints and corporate greenwashing, for the claim that the concept came from BP marketing.

1ZTJ9omXOQ0.summary: Chandler Carruth's CppNow 2023 talk describes Carbon as a successor language to C++ rather than a superset, focusing on C++ interop and a path to memory safety in large existing codebases. It explains why Carbon takes a different approach from Cpp2 and Circle.
1ZTJ9omXOQ0.why: HN cites it as the authoritative statement of Carbon's memory safety plans, including its borrow-checker-like direction.

1ZTRb-2DZGs.summary: Justine Tunney presents Redbean, a web server distributed as a single actually portable executable that runs on multiple operating systems. It embeds Lua, SQLite and MbedTLS in a fork-based server.
1ZTRb-2DZGs.why: The author and others link it as the definitive explanation of redbean and the APE toolchain, including its performance claims.

1cUUfMeOijg.summary: Tom Scott visits Cloudflare's San Francisco office to show the wall of lava lamps whose camera feed is used as a source of entropy for random number generation. It is a short explainer on how this helps secure internet encryption.
1cUUfMeOijg.why: The go-to short explanation whenever lava lamps, entropy sources, or Cloudflare randomness come up.

1eIxUuuJX7Y.summary: Adam Something gives a short, tongue-in-cheek defense of Soviet-era prefab apartment blocks. He argues they offer efficient, dense housing with schools and services built nearby.
1eIxUuuJX7Y.why: Linked in housing and urbanism threads as a fun, deliberately provocative case that dense blocks are better than their reputation.

1fZTOjd_bOQ.summary: Scott Jenson, a veteran UX designer formerly at Apple and Google, argues that the 'UX/UI' split pits programmers against designers and narrows ambition in open source. He makes the case that desktop UX has stagnated and that open source projects could lead experimentation beyond current interaction models.
1fZTOjd_bOQ.why: HN commenters cite it when discussing stagnating desktop UX, Apple's design decline, and open source's chance to experiment with new interaction models.

1k4x9FrD5k4.summary: Andong examines the popular story that Norway invented salmon sushi in Japan in the 1990s. He argues it is largely a myth, pointing to earlier evidence of raw salmon eaten in Japan and elsewhere.
1k4x9FrD5k4.why: HN cites it as the debunking of the Norway salmon sushi story.

1kQUXpZpLXI.summary: Der8auer visits Tescan and uses an electron microscope to compare real transistor sizes on Intel 14nm and AMD 7nm chips. It shows that process node names do not match physical measurements.
1kQUXpZpLXI.why: HN cites it as visual evidence that nm node names are marketing labels and for its neat electron microscope comparison.

1m0TQjBRcFo.summary: BigClive tears down and tests a germicidal UVC lamp from eBay that floods a room with narrow-band ultraviolet and ozone. He warns of the eye and skin hazards.
1m0TQjBRcFo.why: HN points to BigClive as a source for how cheap UVC lamps actually work and what they emit.

1tQ5XwvjPmA.summary: Recording of the January 1984 Boston Computer Society meeting where Steve Jobs unveiled the Macintosh. It is followed by a panel Q&A with core Mac team members such as Andy Hertzfeld, Bill Atkinson and Steve Capps.
1tQ5XwvjPmA.why: HN points to it as the primary source for the original Mac demo and the personal post-show Q&A with the team.

1vpepaQ-VQQ.summary: Linus Tech Tips warns against cheap Android TV boxes, many of which ship with preinstalled malware. It looks at several boxes and suggests safer alternatives such as Chromecast and Nvidia Shield.
1vpepaQ-VQQ.why: HN cites it as broad, accessible evidence that cheap Android TV boxes often come loaded with malware.

1vui-LupKJI.summary: A PyCon 2013 block of Friday evening lightning talks. It includes the debut of Hy, a Lisp dialect that compiles to Python AST, and Solomon Hykes's first public talk on Docker.
1vui-LupKJI.why: HN links it as the historical source for two projects: Hy's first announcement and the earliest recorded Docker talk.

1wVho3I0NtU.summary: Victor Hugo Morales's famous radio commentary of Maradona's second goal against England at the 1986 World Cup. The emotional call is for many Argentines inseparable from the goal itself.
1wVho3I0NtU.why: HN points to it as the best commentary of the goal, in Spanish, usually after Maradona's death or in discussions of remarkable goals.

128IR21ZQa0.summary: A 2007 Fox news segment that portrays 4chan users as hardcore hackers.
128IR21ZQa0.why: Cited mockingly as an example of sensationalist television coverage of internet culture.

12OSBJwogFc.summary: A Corning-sponsored video in which Adam Savage and Jamie Hyneman introduce flexible, bendable glass. It covers the history of glass innovation with demonstrations of bendable optical fiber and ultra-thin glass.
12OSBJwogFc.why: Pointed to for nice demonstrations of bendable glass, though commenters note it feels like an infomercial.

15HTd4Um1m4.summary: A one-minute clip from South Park in which BP issues a hilariously insincere corporate apology over its oil spill.
15HTd4Um1m4.why: Used as a joke reference whenever a company issues a hollow public apology.

1BB6wj6RyKo.summary: GE Lighting's official how-to for factory resetting C by GE smart bulbs, using a long sequence of precisely timed on and off cycles.
1BB6wj6RyKo.why: HN cites it as a prime example of absurd, user-hostile IoT reset procedures.

1FwgCRIS0Wg.summary: Ben Felix examines whether the well-known 4% retirement withdrawal rule holds up, drawing on academic papers. He argues that a safe rate may be closer to 2.7%, especially for early retirees.
1FwgCRIS0Wg.why: HN cites it as the source for the argument that safe withdrawal rates should be lower than 4%.

1IOL4q5tDDQ.summary: The Secret of Monkey Island intro theme played through the internal PC speaker. It is a tribute to LucasArts.
1IOL4q5tDDQ.why: HN shares it for nostalgia about the tinny PC speaker sound of early adventure games.

1JpwkeTBwgs.summary: A CBS Evening News report from the 2018 NATO summit, where President Trump criticized Germany over its gas pipeline deal with Russia and pressed allies on defense spending.
1JpwkeTBwgs.why: Linked as the famous clip of Trump scolding Germany over Russian gas, whenever European energy dependence comes up.

1La4QzGeaaQ.summary: A travel video of Peru shot natively in 8K HDR at 60fps on a Red Helium sensor. It covers Lima, the Amazon, Cusco and other places.
1La4QzGeaaQ.why: HN doesn't recommend it for its content but uses it as a handy example of file size and bitrate for high-resolution video.

1QD9XQm_Jd4.summary: Steve Yegge is interviewed at Google's Kirkland office about the birth, growth and future of his Rhino on Rails project, a Rails clone on the Rhino JavaScript engine, and other web development topics.
1QD9XQm_Jd4.why: Mentioned mainly as the place to hear Yegge discuss Rhino on Rails, a project that was never released.

1RPoymt3Jx4.summary: A 1956 episode clip of the game show I've Got a Secret in which 95-year-old Samuel J. Seymour appears as the mystery guest. He was the last living eyewitness to Lincoln's assassination at Ford's Theater, and the panel tries to guess his secret.
1RPoymt3Jx4.why: HN commenters link it whenever Lincoln, the Civil War, or how recent history really is comes up, as striking footage of a living witness to the assassination.

1Rr_XzzJ6gc.summary: A 2018 vlog showing how to use the windshield wipers on a Tesla Model 3, including auto mode, manual settings and voice commands. It is labeled outdated.
1Rr_XzzJ6gc.why: Used in UI debates as evidence that wiper control on the touchscreen is awkward, or alternatively that it is just two touches.

1TCX90yALsI.summary: A very short clip from Star Trek: The Next Generation's 'Peak Performance' in which Picard says it is possible to commit no mistakes and still lose. It is a single quotable moment about how outcomes are not fully in your control.
1TCX90yALsI.why: HN uses it as a quip or shorthand to illustrate that randomness and circumstance can decide outcomes regardless of skill.

1VgptLwP588.summary: Mark Russinovich's closing keynote at Rust Nation UK on Microsoft's adoption of Rust, covering security gains, integration challenges, performance results and lessons learned.
1VgptLwP588.why: Cited for concrete claims about Microsoft's Rust adoption, such as speedups from rewrites and internal C to Rust translation efforts.

1X7fZoDs9KU.summary: Policy advisor Simon Anholt presents the Good Country Index, a measure of how much each nation contributes to the world beyond its own borders. In a funny TED talk he argues governments should think globally, and reveals which countries rank surprisingly.
1X7fZoDs9KU.why: HN points to it as an alternative to GDP for measuring national progress and as background on the Good Country Index.

1YWD6Y9FUuw.summary: A short clip of the Super Mario Bros 3 proof-of-concept PC port built by id Software's founders to pitch Nintendo on a PC version. Nintendo passed, and the same technology led to Commander Keen.
1YWD6Y9FUuw.why: Cited as footage of a famous piece of gaming history whenever id Software, Commander Keen, or scrolling tech comes up.

1_FXVjf46T8.summary: A short SpaceX video of the Dragon 2 pad abort test, in which the capsule's thrusters fire to carry it away from the launch pad. It also shows the pad deluge system.
1_FXVjf46T8.why: HN commenters cite it as evidence that Dragon's built-in launch escape system works and that a failed launch need not kill the crew.

1_OXM4mr_i0.summary: A short clip of the Mythbusters demonstrating superheated water in a microwave, which can erupt violently when disturbed.
1_OXM4mr_i0.why: HN cites it as the standard demonstration of superheated water, in threads about microwaving water and tea.

1_SdC8LVODY.summary: Audio-only recording of the first part of John Carmack's QuakeCon 2010 keynote, taken from G4TV. It covers id Software's work around that time, including Rage and platform topics such as PC, PS3 and Xbox 360, and includes his informal audience poll about paying for mobile apps.
1_SdC8LVODY.why: Cited mainly for Carmack's offhand survey asking how many people had spent $20 on Android apps, used in debates about app store economics.

1kZgG58zz8U.summary: A short South China Morning Post report on Nio's second-generation automated battery-swap stations for electric vehicles. It notes that Nio had built more than 800 stations in China by early 2022.
1kZgG58zz8U.why: Linked as concrete evidence that automated EV battery swapping already works at scale in China.

1kuoS796vNw.summary: A brief demo of the Smalltalk debugger, including defining a method that doesn't exist yet while the program is stopped mid-crash.
1kuoS796vNw.why: HN cites it as a concise demo of live debugging and editing code in a running Smalltalk environment.

1miGzTwK28U.summary: A short clip of molecular biologist Cristina Sanchez describing her lab research on how THC affects cancer cells. It is uploaded on a channel promoting cannabis as a cancer treatment.
1miGzTwK28U.why: HN commenters mostly cite it critically, as the kind of source behind cannabis-cures-cancer claims that overstate early lab results.

1nBx-37c3c8.summary: A short excerpt of Noam Chomsky telling a BBC journalist that he does not accuse him of self-censorship. He argues that people who believed differently would not have been hired into that position.
1nBx-37c3c8.why: HN cites it as a well-known clip on how structural incentives and hiring shape media bias without conspiracy.

1njzgXSzA-A.summary: An official Seinfeld clip explaining the origin of Festivus, the holiday from the show. It looks back at why the Festivus episode came about.
1njzgXSzA-A.why: HN mostly references it for the origin of Festivus or as a seasonal joke.

1qSsVBPh9Lo.summary: A short demonstration of a crow using a purpose-built vending machine, in which the bird exchanges objects for rewards. The creator sells the machine as a kit.
1qSsVBPh9Lo.why: Linked in crow-intelligence threads as concrete evidence that crows can learn to trade coins or tokens for food.

1seNMSamtxM.summary: A short video explaining the Intel Management Engine, a hidden embedded computer inside Intel machines with deep access to hardware. It is presented from an insider's perspective and raises backdoor and NSA concerns.
1seNMSamtxM.why: HN cites it as a quick introduction to why Intel ME is a trust problem for anyone worried about hardware-level access.
